description: Collective-intelligence surveys — a participant is shown an adaptive sample of ideas from a shared pool, selects the ones they prefer, ranks them, contributes one of their own, and sees the group's live ranking. Humans take the activity through the rendered form; AI agents take the same activity through MCP tools, into the same pool.

example_prompts.prompt: A survey asking people what our team should focus on next quarter. Show each person 10 ideas and let them pick up to 5.
example_prompts.notes: The canonical activity — one select item with sample 10 and max-choices 5.

example_prompts.prompt: After people pick their favourite ideas, have them drag those into order of importance.
example_prompts.notes: A rank item orders whatever the select before it gathered; it carries no list of its own.

example_prompts.prompt: Let people add one idea of their own after they have voted, but let them skip it.
example_prompts.notes: `optional` is a bare flag — it takes no value.

example_prompts.prompt: Show the top 10 ideas with their scores and how many people have taken part.
example_prompts.notes: limit 10 with show-scores and show-participants, both bare flags.

example_prompts.prompt: A complete flow: welcome, choose, rank, contribute, results, thanks.
example_prompts.produces: start, select, rank, contribute, results, thanks
example_prompts.notes: Each kind may appear once; start opens the activity and thanks closes it.

example_prompts.prompt: A survey that both people and AI agents can take, showing everyone the human ranking.
example_prompts.notes: participants ["human" "agent"] on the activity, audience "human" on the results item.

example_prompts.prompt: A survey people cannot go back through once they have answered.
example_prompts.notes: navigation "linear" — the default, chained after the items list.

example_prompts.prompt: Show each participant 12 ideas and let them select exactly 3.
example_prompts.notes: min-choices 3 max-choices 3; max-choices can never exceed sample.
